data.name: Yuvanraaj
data.gender_notes: Yuvanraaj is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Yuvanraaj is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'yuvan' (young) and 'raaj' (king). It signifies the young king who is yet to claim his throne and rule over his kingdom. The name Yuvanraaj carries the meaning “Young King” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Yuvanraaj usually hope their child will grow to embody young king and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embodiment of youth and royalty, symbolizing leadership and power.
data.etymology: Yuvanraaj belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Young King.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Yuvanraaj total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Yuvanraaj has a rich cultural history as it symbolizes the concept of royalty and honor in Hindu society. This name was often given to the eldest son in a noble family, providing him with an early sense of responsibility and preparing him to take on the role of the family head upon the father's retirement or passing.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Yuvanraaj represents the manifestation of inner authority and leadership in the individual. It signifies a young person who is destined to lead and rule, but who is also expected to uphold the dharma (duty) and maintain balance in his or her personal and social life. This name serves as a reminder that one's journey towards spiritual growth is intimately connected to the roles and responsibilities assumed in life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Yuvanraaj: Young King. This name symbolizes the innate leadership and wisdom of a youth, who rules with compassion and grace. It is a call to embrace one's potential and lead from the heart.

vedic_reference.note: This name is derived from the Sanskrit words युवा (yuvā) and राज (rāj), meaning 'young king'.

historical_references.reference: Yuvanraj Chodasen was the eldest son and successor of Chodasen I of the Choda Dynasty in South India. He ruled from 1070 CE to 1095 CE.
Another Yuvanraj, Yuvanraj Chola I, was the eldest son of the great Chola Emperor Rajaraja Chola I. He ruled from 1014 CE to 1044 CE.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Yuvanraaj' which means 'Prince' in Sanskrit, has seen a modern resurgence in various contexts. In the entertainment industry, there is a trend of using traditional names for characters in movies and television shows. For instance, the Tamil film 'Kabali' featured a character named 'Yuvan Shankar Raja' who was a playful take on the name 'Yuvanraaj'. In the social media sphere, individuals are reclaiming their traditional names as part of their personal branding. Lastly, in the business world, there is a growing trend of using traditional Indian names for startups and brands. For instance, 'Yuvraaj Foods' and 'Yuvraaj Enterprises' are names of established businesses in India.

name_in_real_life.story: Aditya Yuvanraaj, a teacher in Kolkata, India, shares that their name Yuvanraaj meaning "Young King" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
